commits.message:
perf(review): stop shipping the full payload to load the drafts list

GET /drafts was returning 23.7MB of JSON for 1386 drafts (measured
against production) -- every row's full `payload` column: raw email
text, complete parsed records, everything, none of which the list page
renders. It only shows title/type/status/confidence/sender/date per
row. ~1s server-side just to serialize and send the response, before
the browser even parses it -- and it only gets slower as the drafts
table grows, which it now does continuously with real mail flowing in.

New GET /drafts/summary (list_draft_summaries in app/drafts/service.py)
extracts only the JSON paths the list actually needs -- job_title or
candidate_name, straight in SQL via -> / ->> -- instead of pulling the
whole payload column into Python just to read one field out of it. The
display title itself is now computed server-side (mirrors the frontend's
draftDisplayTitle exactly: job_title for a requirement, the single
consultant's name or a "Hotlist — N consultants" count otherwise),
so the response never needs a payload at all.

DraftListPage now calls this instead of the old GET /drafts. Nothing
else changes: same filters, same client-side search (now over
display_title instead of computing it from payload), same detail page
(still uses the full GET /drafts/{id} for editing, unchanged).

Registered ahead of GET /drafts/{draft_id} so "summary" is never
swallowed as a draft_id path param.

New coverage: the summary response never includes `payload`; a job
requirement's title comes from its record's job_title; a one-consultant
hotlist shows the candidate's name, a multi-consultant one shows a
count. Full regression suite (18 checks) green; frontend type-checks
and builds clean.
